# LUMEN — results

*Generated by `scripts/step08_report.py` on 2026-10-22 19:13 UTC from the tables in `tables/` (commit c2653e5). Do not edit by hand. The protocol was pre-registered in `METHOD_NOTES.md` at commit 4f7c6b4, before any model was scored on real folds.*

## Headline findings

- **LOSO.** A4 has the lower per-soil MAE than: mean-of-others 12/13 (sig. better 10, sig. worse 0); PLS 12/13 (sig. better 9, sig. worse 0); ridge 12/13 (sig. better 7, sig. worse 0); RF 12/13 (sig. better 1, sig. worse 0); RF-raw 12/13 (sig. better 2, sig. worse 0).
  - A4 is the single best method (of 11) on 1/13 targets: logIsFeO.
  - Another method is best on: PLG (A2_pretrain_real), LCP (A3_pretrain_mixup), HCP (A2_pretrain_real), OLV (RF), ILM (A2_pretrain_real), AGG (A2_pretrain_real), OTH (A2_pretrain_real), FeO (A3_pretrain_mixup), TiO2 (A2_pretrain_real), Al2O3 (A2_pretrain_real), CaO (A2_pretrain_real), MgO (A1m_scratch_mixup).
- **LOMO.** A4 has the lower per-soil MAE than: mean-of-others 11/13 (sig. better 9, sig. worse 0); PLS 11/13 (sig. better 1, sig. worse 0); ridge 11/13 (sig. better 2, sig. worse 0); RF 10/13 (sig. better 3, sig. worse 0); RF-raw 10/13 (sig. better 3, sig. worse 0).
  - A4 is the single best method (of 11) on 4/13 targets: PLG, ILM, AGG, FeO.
  - Another method is best on: LCP (A2_pretrain_real), HCP (A2_pretrain_real), OLV (RF), OTH (mean-of-others), TiO2 (A2_pretrain_real), Al2O3 (A0_zero_shot), CaO (A0_zero_shot), MgO (A1_scratch_real), logIsFeO (A2_pretrain_real).
- **Ablations (LOSO).** The pre-registered primary A4 (pretrain + mixup + replay) is *not* the best configuration: A2 (pretrain + real spectra only) has the lower MAE on 12/13 targets (0 Holm-significant either way). Pretraining helps (A2 below A1 on 13/13); SSA-mixup + replay did not (A4 below A2 on 1/13, A3 below A2 on 3/13). Zero-shot A0 is the worst LUMEN variant (composition MAE 9.1 vs 2.7 vol % for A4).
- **Ablations (LOMO).** The pre-registered primary A4 (pretrain + mixup + replay) is *not* the best configuration: A2 (pretrain + real spectra only) has the lower MAE on 8/13 targets (0 Holm-significant either way). Pretraining helps (A2 below A1 on 7/13); SSA-mixup + replay did not (A4 below A2 on 5/13, A3 below A2 on 1/13). Zero-shot A0 is the worst LUMEN variant (composition MAE 9.1 vs 4.7 vol % for A4).
- **Identifiability gate.** 11 of 13 targets pass: PLG, LCP, HCP, ILM, AGG, FeO, TiO2, Al2O3, CaO, MgO, logIsFeO. Withheld from the M³ maps: OLV, OTH. Under LOMO the skill CI also includes 0 for: OLV, AGG, OTH.
- **Fairness note for the next two items.** Korokhin's and Jung's methods never see an LSCC soil (physics-only inversions); LUMEN A4 is fine-tuned on the 18 (LOSO) or fewer (LOMO) other soils. The like-for-like physics-only comparison is LUMEN A0 (zero-shot).
- **Korokhin 2024** (5-mineral proportions, 19 soils, LOSO).
  - A4 vs their Nelder–Mead fit: CPX 2.24 vs 5.30, OPX 3.25 vs 8.37, OLV 1.91 vs 7.44, PLG 5.55 vs 12.08, ILM 2.39 vs 5.24. A4 is lower on 5/5; Holm-significant on: CPX, OPX, OLV, PLG, ILM.
  - A4 vs the mean of the other soils: lower on 5/5; Holm-significant on: CPX, OPX, PLG, ILM.
  - Zero-shot A0 (physics-only, like-for-like) vs their fit: lower on 3/5 (CPX 8.18 vs 5.30, OPX 8.98 vs 8.37, OLV 2.58 vs 7.44, PLG 10.40 vs 12.08, ILM 3.06 vs 5.24); Holm-significant on: OLV.
- **Korokhin 2024** (5-mineral proportions, 19 soils, LOMO).
  - A4 vs their Nelder–Mead fit: CPX 3.14 vs 5.30, OPX 6.86 vs 8.37, OLV 2.50 vs 7.44, PLG 12.64 vs 12.08, ILM 4.06 vs 5.24. A4 is lower on 4/5; Holm-significant on: OLV.
  - A4 vs the mean of the other soils: lower on 4/5; Holm-significant on: CPX, OPX, PLG, ILM.
  - Maturity, pooled 19 soils, Spearman ρ vs measured Is/FeO per fraction (LOSO): LUMEN 0.72 / 0.81 / 0.96; Korokhin nFe 0.55 / 0.37 / 0.44.
- **Jung 2026** (4 soils at 20–45 µm, LOSO). A4 meets 4 of the 4 claim variants: olivine < 7: 1.00 (Jung 5.78, prior-only 1.76); ilmenite < 10 (15071 excepted): 1.24 (Jung 17.56, prior-only 10.87); ilmenite < 10: 1.24 (Jung 22.13, prior-only 10.87); plagioclase < 30: 7.95 (Jung 16.83, prior-only 16.92).
- **Jung 2026** (4 soils at 20–45 µm, LOMO). A4 meets 4 of the 4 claim variants: olivine < 7: 2.10 (Jung 5.78, prior-only 1.76); ilmenite < 10 (15071 excepted): 3.99 (Jung 17.56, prior-only 10.87); ilmenite < 10: 3.99 (Jung 22.13, prior-only 10.87); plagioclase < 30: 10.72 (Jung 16.83, prior-only 16.92).
  - With n = 4 soils this is weak evidence. Zero-shot A0 also meets 4/4, while the mean of the other soils meets 1/4.
  - Maturity on the same 4 soils: Pearson r = 0.99 for LUMEN Is/FeO vs -0.00 for Jung's I_sm; MAE 4.8 vs 19.7 Is/FeO units.
- **Fernández-Díaz 2026** FeO (LOSO): A4 MAE 1.256 wt % vs FD as published (AE→RF, M³-trained AE) 2.169 (paired p = 0.023, Holm over the 12 FD variants 0.069) and the best FD variant FD-wavelet/SVR-RBF 1.913 (p = 0.009, Holm 0.057). A4 is lower than all 12 FD variants; 3/12 survive Holm. Best classic: RF 2.132.
- **Fernández-Díaz 2026** FeO (LOMO): A4 MAE 2.589 wt % vs FD as published (AE→RF, M³-trained AE) 3.482 (paired p = 0.018, Holm over the 12 FD variants 0.163) and the best FD variant FD-AE-synth/SVR-lin 2.910 (p = 0.490, Holm 0.980). A4 is lower than all 12 FD variants; 1/12 survive Holm. Best classic: RF-raw 3.447.
- **Coverage** (LOSO, mean over targets, 68/90/95 %): raw ensemble 0.59/0.82/0.89; normalised conformal 0.68/0.90/0.95.
- **Coverage** (LOMO, mean over targets, 68/90/95 %): raw ensemble 0.33/0.55/0.64; normalised conformal 0.64/0.86/0.92.
- **M³ landing sites (Addendum A, 18 sites).** LUMEN does *not* transfer to orbital spectra: FeO MAE 6.36 wt % (bias -5.7) with no site training, worse than the mean of the other sites (3.70); 3.56 after leave-one-site-out recalibration, against 3.07 for the best Fernández-Díaz variant (FD-AE-M3/SVR-lin), 3.48 for FD as published and 3.18 for a band ratio. Best R² of any method 0.27.

### Hand-off open issue 1 — the k round trip

The k round-trip failure came from **c1sc50** (class HGL, d_eff 50 µm), not from ilmenite.

- 13 bands at 0.54–0.87 µm are darker (min R = 0.0231) than the slab model at k = 1 (R = 0.0360).
- R(k) is non-monotonic: it has an opacity floor (R = 0.0157), so the old [1e-9, 1] bracket clamped these bands to k = 1.
- With the root taken on the falling branch, k_max is now 0.0020 and the round trip is 1.9e-13.

### Coverage of the real data (sim-to-real gap)

Real spectra lie inside the synthetic cloud:

- median nearest-neighbour distance 0.102 vs 0.144 synthetic-to-synthetic;
- 4 % of real spectra lie beyond the synthetic 95th percentile.

They are nonetheless separable:

- real-vs-synthetic AUC: logistic 0.952, random forest 0.971;
- against noise-free synthetic spectra: 0.976 / 0.993.

The gap is physical, not a noise artefact.

## 5. Head-to-head comparisons (step06)

### Korokhin et al. (2024)

5-mineral proportions (CPX = HCP, OPX = LCP, OLV, PLG, ILM; % of their sum), scored exactly as their reproduction scores itself:

- per-soil means over the <10 / 10–20 / 20–45 µm fractions;
- the mean-of-other-soils baseline is fraction-matched within the scored set;
- MAE in percentage points.

Their truth takes the pyroxene split straight from LSCC Table 2; ours rescales it to the Table 1 pyroxene total. Every method is scored against *their* truth. The definitional gap is small (mean |Δ| 0.02–0.22 pp, max 3.78 pp, at 61141 and 62231), and the same comparison against our truth is in `tables/step06_korokhin_mae.csv` (`truth = lumen_truth`).

## 7. Deviations from the pre-registration

1. **Korokhin truth definition (clarification of D18, before any LUMEN result existed).**
   The Korokhin reproduction takes the pyroxene split from LSCC Table 2 as printed. step01
   rescales it to the Table 1 pyroxene total, which keeps the 7-part composition closed.
   - The two 5-mineral truths differ by a mean of ≤ 0.23 pp per mineral, and by more than
     1 pp only for 61141 (<10, 10–20 µm) and 62231 (10–20 µm), where Table 2's pyroxene
     sum disagrees with Table 1.
   - Following D18 ("scored the way that paper scores itself"), every method in the
     Korokhin comparison is scored against **their** truth. The comparison against our
     truth is reported as a sensitivity.
   - The gap was found by a dry run of the evaluation code on placeholder predictions.
2. **Run order (no effect on results).**
   - step03 was restarted once, with the FD autoencoder pinned to one CPU thread, to stop
     it starving the concurrent pretraining. It had not yet written any output, and the
     rerun used the same seeds.
   - Fine-tuning started about 10 minutes late because of a process-wait bug in the
     launcher.
   - The fine-tuning pool was restarted once, from 3 to 4 workers. Finished jobs were kept,
     after checking every saved job file, and each job's seed depends only on (protocol,
     fold, configuration, member).
3. **Holm over the Fernández-Díaz variants (more conservative than pre-registered).**
   - D18 specified paired Wilcoxon tests of A4 against every FD variant.
   - The report additionally applies a Holm correction over the 12 variants, and shows the
     raw p alongside.
4. **Optional extension, run later as Addendum A.** The M³ landing-site validation (hand-off
   §6.8) was first blocked because the network policy denied planetarydata.jpl.nasa.gov.
   - Once the host was allowed, it was pre-registered (Addendum A) and run as step00b
     (staging) and step10 (scoring).
   - It is FeO only: the ground truth has no TiO₂.
5. **Paper draft generated from the tables.**
   - `PAPER_DRAFT.md` is assembled by `scripts/step09_paper.py` from hand-written sections
     in `paper/` and numbers read from `tables/`.
   - Every directional claim in the prose is asserted against the numbers before the draft
     is written.

## Addendum A — M³ landing-site validation (pre-registered before any site spectrum was fetched)

Added after the main study, when the PDS host became reachable. It is the hand-off's §6.8:
a quantitative test of LUMEN on real orbital spectra, against Fernández-Díaz et al.
(2026) on their own task. Everything below was fixed before any site spectrum was
downloaded.

- **D20 sites and truth.**
  - The 50 returned samples of `data/ground_truth/fernandez2026_ground_truth_50.csv`
    (FD's ground truth, FeO only) are grouped by distinct (lat, lon). One **site** is one
    coordinate, and its truth is the mean FeO of its samples.
  - All statistics are over sites, so FD's pseudo-replicates are never counted twice.
  - Coordinates are used exactly as FD lists them. Where FD gives samples from different
    stations the same coordinate (Apollo 17 LM vs LRV station 1), the site mixes them;
    this is flagged, not corrected.
- **D21 M³ spectra.**
  - **Candidate strips:** every global-mode L2 strip in `CH1M3_0004/INDEX/L2_INDEX.TAB`
    (806 products).
  - **Footprints:** probed from each strip's L1B LOC file (5 lines; range requests).
  - **Inclusion:** a strip covers a site if its nearest pixel is within 0.01° of the site
    and at least 5 samples from either swath edge.
  - **Strip spectrum:** the 3 × 3-pixel mean around the nearest pixel, after dropping
    pixels with any non-finite, ≤ 0 or ≥ 1 reflectance. A strip contributes only if
    ≥ 5 / 9 pixels remain.
  - **Site spectrum:** the per-band median over the contributing strips. Every method uses
    this spectrum. Sites with no contributing strip are reported and excluded.
  - **Storage:** the fetched spectra and their provenance are staged into
    `data/m3_sites/` by `scripts/step00b_fetch_m3_sites.py`, and the manifest is
    regenerated.
- **D22 methods** (FeO).
  - **LUMEN-M3 (primary)** — the A4 ensemble, applied with Korokhin Eq. 2 and **no M³
    training data**:
    - for an Apollo site of mission X, the 5 A4 LOMO members that held out mission X, so
      no soil from that mission was seen. Their weights are regenerated by re-running the
      identical fine-tuning jobs, and reproducibility is checked against the stored
      step04 predictions;
    - for Luna and Chang'e sites, the final all-soil ensemble.
  - **LUMEN-M3 + site recalibration** — leave-one-site-out OLS, y = a + b·ŷ, fit on the
    other sites. It uses the same information as the trained baselines.
  - **FD as published** — M³ bands 3–85 (83 bands), unscaled L2 reflectance; db4 level-2
    periodization, A2 + D2 (42 coefficients).
    - Autoencoder 42 → 32 → 16 → 6 → … trained unsupervised on the Shapley-scene pixels
      (same architecture and schedule as D14).
    - Regressors Lasso / SVR-lin / SVR-RBF / RF with the Table 5 grids.
    - Training rows are the samples of the other sites (as FD train on samples); inner
      GroupKFold by site; leave-one-site-out.
  - **FD no-AE** — the same with the 42 coefficients directly.
  - **Band ratio** — θ = arctan((R950 / R750 − 1.19) / (R750 − 0.08)) (Lucey et al.
    2000 origin), on the M³ bands nearest 750 and 950 nm, mapped to FeO by a
    leave-one-site-out linear fit.
  - **Mean of the other sites.**
- **D23 scoring.**
  - MAE, RMSE and R² over sites.
  - Paired Wilcoxon on per-site absolute errors, LUMEN-M3 against each comparator, with
    Holm over the comparators.
  - **Primary comparison:** LUMEN-M3 vs FD as published (AE → RF).
  - LUMEN's other outputs at the sites (mineralogy, TiO₂, maturity) are reported without
    truth.
  - Expected difficulties, stated in advance:
    - Chang'e-5 (FeO 22.5 wt %) lies above every LSCC soil (max 18.5), so LUMEN must
      extrapolate there;
    - one landing-site pixel per site is a small, noisy target.

## Addendum B — exact CV+ and M³ destriping (pre-registered before running)

These close the two remaining open items of the hand-off.

- **D24 exact CV+ (step11).** For every unordered pair of soils {i, j}, the 5 A4 members are
  fine-tuned without both soils: 171 pairs × 5 = 855 jobs. The recipe and seeds rule are
  those of D11; the seed hashes the pair.
  - For test soil j, the calibration scores of soil i come from model M_{ij}, which saw
    neither soil:
    - absolute residuals R = |y_i − μ_ij(x_i)| (per spectrum);
    - normalised residuals R / σ_ij(x_i).
  - CV+ interval for each spectrum of j (Barber et al. 2021):
    - absolute: [q_lo{μ_ij(x_j) − R}, q_hi{μ_ij(x_j) + R}] over every calibration spectrum
      of every i ≠ j;
    - normalised: the analogue with σ_ij(x_j) scaling.
  - The same is done for LOMO with the 15 mission pairs (75 jobs).
  - Coverage at 68 / 90 / 95 % is reported beside the approximate intervals of D17.
- **D25 M³ destriping (step07 sensitivity).** For every band, the along-track mean of each
  sample column is divided by a 31-sample running median of those column means, and each
  column is divided by that ratio. This is a column-gain flat field; it preserves the
  scene's large-scale signal.
  - The Shapley maps and the Korokhin map comparison are recomputed on the destriped cube
    and reported as a sensitivity.
  - The undestriped maps stay primary, as pre-registered in D19.
